specGaps: GAP (question origin, submit_test exhaustion): §2.11's origin vocabulary is closed (surface-tool | plan-review-cap | debug-architecture | implementer-blocked | review-round-cap | scope-conflict) and names no test-repair origin, yet §3.3 requires submit_test to write a question at testRepairAttempts exhaustion. PROPOSED (no widening): origin 'implementer-blocked' — the blocked write-capable sub-session here IS the test-writer, the origin's literal meaning. Raise at the Phase 9 milestone gate + CORRECTIONS.md.

GAP (vet round-cap outcome): the plan says only 'mustFix loops bounded by vetMaxRounds' and never states the at-cap behaviour. PROPOSED (mirrors both sibling caps — §3.3 reviewMaxRounds 'cap => question + blocked' and the submit-side exhaustion): the item STAYS at RED, store.setBlocked {stage:'TEST_VETTED', reason naming vetMaxRounds, questionId}, ONE §2.11 question with origin 'review-round-cap' (the vet loop is a review-round cap over the test; no vocabulary widening) and blocksItems [itemId].

GAP (immediate-pass aftermath): the plan pins 'rejected and records the ponytail-skip decision' but not the item's resulting annotations or the record's §2.7 shape. PROPOSED: the item remains PENDING, un-blocked, no question (the orchestrator chooses conductor_defer or a re-dispatch); the handler appends a kind:'derived' §2.7 record with the two REAL scored options the plan itself names — 'behavior-already-exists (ponytail rung skip; item may be unnecessary)' vs 'test-is-wrong (rewrite and resubmit)' — choice 'test-is-wrong' as the conservative default (the rejection already forces resubmission; skip stays available via conductor_defer reading the ledger). >=2 scored options keeps this consistent with decide.requireTwoOptions.

GAP (test-writer reply schema): §2.10 defines no test-writer output schema, but the fan-out engine requires a schemaName per dispatch. PROPOSED (no new schema): every testWriter dispatch uses SCHEMAS.ImplementerResult — its status vocabulary (DONE | DONE_WITH_CONCERNS | NEEDS_CONTEXT | BLOCKED) is exactly what the repair loop consumes; the deliverable is the test file the responder writes, the structured reply is the status envelope.

GAP (who dispatches the initial test-writer): §3.3 assigns the test-writer sub-session to the PENDING->RED stage and §3.4 makes conductor_submit_test that stage's tool, but no line says the handler performs the FIRST writer dispatch. PROPOSED: handleSubmitTest owns the whole stage — initial testWriter dispatch (role 'testWriter', writeCapable:true, tree 'main' until 9.6 worktrees), then the handler-run test, then the bounded repair loop — since the 9.4c wave driver only sequences stage tools and 'the handler returns the failure to the writer' presumes the handler holds the writer conversation.

GAP (stale red between vet rounds): §3.3 gives the vet critics 'the captured red output', but after a mustFix repair changes the test the captured red is stale. PROPOSED (derived from §3.3's changed-test rule 'the changed test re-enters the test discipline'): after every mustFix repair the handler re-runs the item test via evidence.runTest and requires a still-legal §2.6.1 red BEFORE re-vetting, so each vet round's prompt carries a true red for the test it is judging; a repair that breaks the red (class 'error' or pass) is handled by the submit-side rules, not vetted.

GAP (writer BLOCKED mid-loop): the §3.3 implementer-status escalation protocol is written for the TEST_VETTED->GREEN implementer; a testWriter replying status 'BLOCKED' inside submit_test's repair loop is unspecified. PROPOSED: exit the loop early into the same exhaustion path (setBlocked + §2.11 question, origin 'implementer-blocked' — literally true here) rather than burning the remaining attempts on a writer that has declared it cannot proceed. No assertion row requires this; recorded for the implementer and the milestone gate.

assertions.text: handleSubmitTest (conductor_submit_test {itemId}) owns the PENDING->RED stage: legality first (gates-phase), then it dispatches the test-writer sub-session through the injected Fanout (role 'testWriter', writeCapable:true, schema ImplementerResult per the pinned specGaps resolution), then THE HANDLER — not the model — runs the item test via adapter/evidence.ts runTest; exit!=0 with failureClass 'assertion' is a legal red: the item advances PENDING->RED through core legalItemTransition, the §2.6 red record lands on evidence.jsonl (written by runTest, that file's only writer), and the tool returns a compact result naming exit code + failureClass + excerpt — the new state asserted by reading the persisted item file via store.loadItem, never a log line

GREENFIELD legal red: a fixture repo whose test imports a module inside the item's declared fileScope that DOES NOT EXIST yet yields failureClass 'missing-subject' (classified by core classifyFailure inside the real evidence.runTest — not stubbed) and is ACCEPTED as a legal RED exactly like 'assertion' — the §2.6.1 case that makes ordinary TDD possible at all; PENDING->RED advances and the evidence record carries failureClass 'missing-subject'

failureClass 'error' (fixture: the test itself is broken — stderr shape with no legal-red class) is REJECTED as a red: no transition occurs; the handler returns the captured failure to the test-writer as a repair re-dispatch whose prompt carries the failure excerpt, bounded by config.workflow.testRepairAttempts — asserted by counting the fake SDK's recorded testWriter dispatches: a writer that repairs the test on attempt 2 reaches RED, and the REPAIR dispatch count never exceeds testRepairAttempts (so total testWriter dispatches never exceed 1 + testRepairAttempts: the initial write is not a repair)

when testRepairAttempts is exhausted with the red still illegal, the handler sets blocked:{stage:'RED', reason, questionId} via store.setBlocked AND writes exactly ONE §2.11 question via adapter/questions.appendQuestion whose blocksItems names exactly this item (origin per the pinned specGaps resolution: 'implementer-blocked') — asserted by READING the persisted item file (state remains PENDING; blocked is an annotation, not a state) and questions.jsonl

an immediately-PASSING test (exit 0) is REJECTED: PENDING->RED is refused (fsm-item redEvidenceGate — a passing test is not a red), the item stays PENDING and UN-blocked, and the handler records the ponytail-skip fork as a §2.7 decision record (kind 'derived', >=2 scored options per the pinned specGaps resolution: behavior-already-exists/rung-skip vs test-is-wrong) through the existing torn-line-safe mintDecisionId/appendDecision helpers, journaling the existing state:decision.recorded event; the compact return names the fork so the orchestrator can conductor_defer or re-dispatch

conductor_submit_test for a behavioral:false item is ILLEGAL: the handler denies at the legality step — consistent with gates-phase nextStageTool, which offers conductor_mark_green for a non-behavioral PENDING, and the deny message names conductor_mark_green as the legal path — BEFORE any dispatch or persisted write: zero fake-SDK calls recorded, the item file byte-identical, no evidence record appended

MANDATORY DEFERRED BINDING 9.4a/5.3 (HANDOFF 'Deferred bindings'): dependency-readiness is enforced CONSISTENTLY by gate and handler, pinned decision ENFORCE (no recovery bypass): (a) core/gates-phase.ts legalTools no longer offers a stage tool for a dependency-unready item — in a two-item fixture where I2 dependsOn I1 and I1 is not yet PUBLISHED, the EXECUTING legal set contains NO conductor_submit_test/conductor_vet_test entry targeting I2 (while I1's own stage tool is still offered), matching schedule.nextWave's deps-PUBLISHED readiness rule; and (b) a DIRECT handleSubmitTest/handleVetTest call for I2 is DENIED naming the unpublished dependency, before any dispatch or write — both surfaces asserted against the SAME fixture so gate and handler provably agree

handleVetTest (conductor_vet_test {itemId}) fans out exactly readFanout('vet', config) critics (vetCritics clamped to parallel.maxReaders) as ONE parallel group via fanout.dispatchWave — role 'reviewer', writeCapable:false, schemaName 'TestVet', fresh sub-sessions (one session.create per critic on the fake) — and every critic's received prompt contains the item spec (title + acceptance), the test content, and the captured red output, and does NOT contain the implementation: the fixture plants a distinctive marker string in a fileScope production file and that marker is asserted ABSENT from every recorded fake prompt (critics cannot be anchored by code that already passes — none exists)

a vet round in which any critic returns a non-empty mustFix routes the UNION of mustFix items back to the test-writer (one write-capable re-dispatch whose prompt carries the mustFix list), re-runs the repaired test through evidence.runTest requiring a still-legal §2.6.1 red before re-vetting (pinned specGaps resolution — the next round's prompt carries a TRUE captured red), then re-vets; the loop is bounded by config.workflow.vetMaxRounds (the knob distinct from reviewMaxRounds) — fake returns mustFix in round 1 and clean verdicts in round 2 => TEST_VETTED with exactly 2 vet rounds and exactly 1 writer re-dispatch in the recorded call log

a vet round in which EVERY critic returns empty mustFix advances RED->TEST_VETTED through core legalItemTransition, persists via store.saveItem (asserted by re-loading the item file), journals through closed-vocabulary events only (fsm:transition / state:item.updated — driven through the REAL throwing journal, no vocabulary widening), and returns a compact result summarizing the per-criterion verdicts

reaching vetMaxRounds with mustFix still outstanding leaves the item at state RED and sets blocked:{stage:'TEST_VETTED', reason naming vetMaxRounds, questionId} plus exactly ONE §2.11 question (origin per the pinned specGaps resolution: 'review-round-cap') whose blocksItems names the item — asserted by reading the persisted item file and questions.jsonl, mirroring the submit-side exhaustion row; no further critic or writer dispatch occurs after the cap

Spec-gap resolutions APPROVED as proposed, with these rulings: (1) question origin at submit_test repair exhaustion uses the EXISTING 'implementer-blocked' and the vet cap uses the EXISTING 'review-round-cap' — the §2.11 origin vocabulary is CLOSED and widening it would be a STOP-AND-PARK, so reusing the closest legal origin is correct; both are raised at the Phase 9 gate. (2) The test-writer reply uses the already-registered SCHEMAS.ImplementerResult — 9.4a authors NO new schema (unlike 9.2, where SCHEMAS.Plan was forced by fanout's mandatory schemaName). (3) The 9.4a/5.3 deferred binding is ENFORCE, not warn: gates-phase legalTools must not offer a stage tool for a dependency-unready item, and the handler must refuse it too — gate and handler consistent, no recovery bypass. All 11 rows keep coveredByTest:null until the test file exists. CORRECTION (orchestrator, post-draft): testRepairAttempts bounds REPAIRS, not total dispatches. Plan §3.3 says the handler 'returns the failure to the writer FOR REPAIR, bounded at testRepairAttempts', and §2.1 comments the knob 'submit_test: illegal-red repair attempts'. So the budget is 1 initial write + up to testRepairAttempts repairs. An earlier draft of this row said total dispatches <= testRepairAttempts, which silently made the knob mean something its own name denies — the same class of defect as C-030's trivialMaxFiles conflation, so it is corrected here rather than pinned into the tests.
